sections.heading: C — Vehicle equipment (Utah Section 15)
sections.markdown:
## C — Vehicle equipment (Utah Section 15)

FACT_ID: sec15-F01 | anchor: A01
Driver-assist safety features only assist the driver and never drive the vehicle, so the driver must stay engaged and focused at all times [A01]
Why it matters: core responsibility rule; driver remains liable despite alerts or automation.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec15-F02 | anchor: A01
Parking assist and cruise control are banned during the driving skills test [A01]
Why it matters: test-day trap; candidate must perform without those aids.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec15-F03 | anchor: A01
Assist features can fail in rain, snow, ice, fog, hills and curves, so the driver must read the manual, know limits, keep sensors clean and software current [A01]
Why it matters: explains when technology cannot be trusted.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec15-F04 | anchor: A01
Every motor vehicle needs brakes on all wheels meeting federal standards, except a truck or truck tractor with three or more axles which may omit brakes on the front wheels [A01]
Why it matters: exact exception is highly testable.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec15-F05 | anchor: A01
With ABS brakes the driver must apply steady firm pressure and must not pump the pedal in a skid [A01]
Why it matters: pumping defeats ABS; common misconception.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec15-F06 | anchor: A02
A bus, RV or trailer at least 80 inches wide needs two amber front clearance lights plus one on each front side, and two red rear clearance lights plus one on each rear side, visible from 500 feet at night [A02]
Why it matters: width threshold plus color-position-distance triple.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F07 | anchor: A02
A load sticking out four feet or more past the bed or body needs two rear flags by day or two rear lights by night, where flags are at least 12 inches square and lights are visible from at least 500 feet [A02]
Why it matters: day versus night requirement with two numbers.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F08 | anchor: A02
Trucks, truck tractors and buses must carry three flares, red emergency reflectors or red electric lights plus two red flags with stands, visible from at least 600 feet, with flares able to burn 12 hours and fuses meeting explosive-bureau standards and burning at least 15 minutes [A02]
Why it matters: dense quantity-distance-time cluster; explosives vehicles may not use flares or fuses.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F09 | anchor: A02
Except motorcycles, every vehicle needs two white headlights, one per side, reaching 350 feet on high beam and 100 feet on low beam, plus a high-beam indicator [A02]
Why it matters: paired distances are classic exam numbers.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F10 | anchor: A02
Every motor vehicle needs one working horn audible from at least 200 feet under normal conditions [A02]
Why it matters: single minimum-distance fact.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F11 | anchor: A02
Every vehicle needs one white rear plate light that makes the plate readable from at least 50 feet [A02]
Why it matters: smallest distance in this section.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F12 | anchor: A02
Mud flaps or guards are required on vehicles rated 10500 pounds or more, vehicles with altered suspension or tire size, and trailers unladen 750 pounds or more, made at least as wide as the tires [A02]
Why it matters: three applicability triggers with two weights.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F13 | anchor: A03
Factory pollution-control equipment must be kept as effective as the original, except propane vehicles whose emissions meet all standards [A03]
Why it matters: maintenance duty plus fuel exception.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec15-F14 | anchor: A03
Red or blue lights showing from the front are reserved for emergency, school, snow-removal and other authorized vehicles, and only authorized emergency vehicles may carry sirens, whistles or bells [A03]
Why it matters: color plus authorized-user restriction.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec15-F15 | anchor: A03
Vehicles need one amber reflector on each front side and one red reflector on each rear side, visible from 500 feet at night and mounted 15 to 60 inches high, with vehicles 30 feet or longer also needing a center amber reflector on each side [A03]
Why it matters: color-position-height-distance plus length trigger.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec15-F16 | anchor: A03
Turn signals need two rear red, yellow or amber lamps and two front white, yellow or amber lamps visible from 100 feet in sunlight, excused only on pre-1953 vehicles under 80 inches wide [A03]
Why it matters: color sets plus visibility and age-width exception.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0102]

High-yield (ranked): 1) brakes and ABS technique [A01]; 2) headlight and signal distances and colors [A02]; 3) wide-vehicle and load lights and flares [A02]; 4) ADAS responsibility and test ban [A01]; 5) horn, plate, reflector and authorized-light rules [A02] [A03].
Misconceptions: ABS should be pumped; assist features can drive alone; any vehicle may show front red-blue lights; one headlight is enough; flares suit every cargo.
Mnemonics: Amber Ahead, Red Rear for clearance, reflector and side-marker colors; 350-100 for high-low beams; 600 for emergency flares, 500 for most rear and side lights.
Glossary: clearance lights (wide-vehicle outline lamps); side markers (side-facing width lamps); reflectors (passive night markers); parking brake (separate holding brake); ADAS (driver-assist safety features).
